record.paper_title: Problèmes ouverts en théorie des intersections
record.original_question: Assume that a natural λ-structure has been constructed on K'(X). For a proper morphism f:X→Y of complete intersection type, and more generally for a relative scheme X over a locally ringed topos Y satisfying the corresponding relative hypotheses, can one prove a Grothendieck-Riemann-Roch formula without projectivity assumptions, using the Todd class of f defined from the relative cotangent complex T_f? Can the same ideas also prove the analogous formula for complex analytic or rigid-analytic spaces, beyond the then-known case of a locally free sheaf on a nonsingular compact complex variety over a point?

evidence.quote: Une fois en possession d'une λ-structure naturelle sur les K'(X), il est possible de formuler le théorème de Riemann-Roch, sous la forme envisagée dans Exp. VIII, pour n'importe quel morphisme f:X→Y propre et d'intersection complète.

Il semble clair que la démonstration de la formule de Riemann-Roch dans ce cas général demandera l'introduction d'idées essentiellement nouvelles, et il est possible que ces mêmes idées pourraient donner la clef d'une démonstration de la formule analogue dans le cas analytique complexe (ou rigide-analytique !).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let f: X → Y be a proper morphism of locally complete intersection type between (suitable) schemes (or, more generally, let X be a relative scheme over a locally ringed topos Y satisfying analogous relative hypotheses). Assume that on the K-theory groups K'(X) of coherent sheaves there is a natural λ-ring structure, and let T_f denote the relative cotangent complex of f. Define the Todd class Td(T_f) of f by means of this relative cotangent complex (via the usual formal series in its Chern classes).

Problem.
(a) Prove a Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch formula of the form
    ch(f_* α) = f_*(ch(α) · Td(T_f))
for every α ∈ K'(X), without assuming that f is projective (i.e., not requiring a factorization through a projective bundle or any global immersion into a smooth Y-scheme).

(b) Establish the analogous formula for proper morphisms in the categories of complex analytic spaces and of rigid analytic spaces, going beyond the case of a single locally free sheaf on a nonsingular compact complex variety mapped to a point.
artifact.status_search_result: The algebraic part has been substantially advanced: O'Brian–Toledo–Tong (1985) established a Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch formula for proper holomorphic maps of complex manifolds; Navarro & Navarro (2017, "On the Riemann–Roch formula without projective hypothesis") proved GRR for proper maps between smooth schemes via A^1-homotopy techniques; and Navarro proved a Riemann–Roch theorem for homotopy-invariant K-theory and projective lci morphisms between finite-dimensional noetherian schemes, without smoothness. Recent works (e.g., Hirzebruch–Riemann–Roch for complex analytic ∞-prestacks, 2026) continue extending the complex/rigid-analytic case. A fully general GRR for arbitrary proper lci morphisms in the relative-topos and rigid-analytic settings as originally envisaged is not uniformly settled, so the problem is best classified as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: On Grothendieck's Riemann-Roch Theorem (Navarro–Navarro)
status_evidence.snippet: GRR extended to proper maps between two smooth schemes via A^1-homotopy theory.
status_evidence.claim: GRR proved without projectivity for proper maps between smooth schemes.

status_evidence.title: Riemann–Roch for homotopy invariant K-theory and Gysin morphisms
status_evidence.snippet: Riemann–Roch for projective lci morphisms between finite-dimensional noetherian schemes, without smoothness, and Gysin morphisms for regular immersions.
status_evidence.claim: Partial extension of GRR to lci morphisms without smoothness.

status_evidence.title: A Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch Formula for Maps of Complex Manifolds (O'Brian, Toledo, Tong)
status_evidence.snippet: GRR formula established for proper holomorphic maps of complex manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: Analytic GRR proved beyond the compact-to-a-point case.

status_evidence.title: Hirzebruch–Riemann–Roch for complex analytic ∞-prestacks
status_evidence.snippet: Cocycle-level HRR identities for complex analytic ∞-prestacks building on O'Brian–Toledo–Tong.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing extensions in the complex analytic setting.
